issues.failure_explanation: The cited trimmed-mean theorem gives failure probability α for ONE fixed vector when k=ln(8/α) rows are removed. Lemma lem:jl_trimming keeps k=ln(8/α) but claims probability 1-α simultaneously for all p points. A union bound over p points then yields failure probability pα, not α. To reach total failure α one must apply the theorem with α/p, i.e. remove k=ln(8p/α) rows. The condition α ≥ 4e^{-cp} also confuses the sample size m with the set size p. Theorem theorem:trim_trip repeats the error with p=|N|, the net size, which is of order the metric entropy (r^d+dnr)·d·ln(·). It claims only k=ln(8n^φ) rows are removed, which is not supported. The claim is in fact false when r exceeds roughly k. A rank-r tensor x=(1/√r)Σ_j a_{i_j}/‖a_{i_j}‖, built from r rows of A, has r rows each with ⟨a_i,x⟩^2≈n^d/(mr). Removing fewer than r rows leaves ‖A^x x‖^2≫1 when m≪n^d, and r is unrestricted in the theorem.

failure_location.quote: The desired result follows by the union bound argument.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the trimming number as k≈ln(8|N|n^φ), i.e. of order the covering entropy (≲ δ²m/C^d rows). Apply the trimmed-mean theorem with α replaced by n^{-φ}/|N|, checking the condition α/|N| ≥ 4e^{-cm}. Restate Lemma lem:jl_trimming (k=ln(8p/α)), Theorem theorem:trim_trip and the informal theorem accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The trimmed-RIP theorem and the headline claim that only ln(8n^φ) rows need to be removed to restore uniform geometry preservation are unsupported and, for larger r, false. The abstract/informal theorem inherits the same quantitative claim. The comparison with i.i.d. sub-Gaussian measurements is also affected.
issues.title: Trimming count k=ln(8/α) / ln(8n^φ) cannot support a union bound over a net or finite set
issues.why_classification: A comparable trimmed-RIP result survives with the same sampling bounds on m and a still-small discarded fraction of rows. The repair needs a contained re-derivation and a changed statement. The advertised 'only ln n rows' scope is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The factor in the statement depends on t through Δ_t, ρ_t, ξ_t, μ_t and A_t, and is raised to the power t+1. The proof only establishes ‖R^{t+1}‖ ≤ α_t‖R^t‖ with iteration-specific α_t. Iterating gives ∏_{s≤t} α_s ‖R^0‖. This does not imply (α_t)^{t+1}‖R^0‖: if early iterates have α_s>1 or are bad while α_t is small, the stated bound can be violated. A uniform bound sup_s α_s would have to be assumed or proven, and Δ_t, ρ_t are not controlled by the paper (the paper itself says ρ_t is hard to control).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bound as ‖R^{t+1}‖ ≤ ∏_{s}α_s‖R^0‖ with α_s the iteration-s factor, or state it under a uniform bound α_s ≤ α.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed convergence-rate statement is not what is proved. Only the one-step contraction (and its product form) holds. This also matters for the claimed convergence guarantee for TrimTIHT.
issues.title: Convergence bound states a power (t+1) of a t-dependent factor but the proof only gives a one-step contraction
issues.why_classification: The proof already yields the correct one-step inequality, so a local restatement as a product or under a uniform bound preserves the argument and conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: To replace √(2ξ_t+ξ_t²)(1+μ_t‖A_t‖√Δ_t) by |1−μ_tΔ_t| one needs 2ξ_t+ξ_t² ≤ |1−μ_tΔ_t|²/(1+μ_t‖A_t‖√Δ_t)² =: s. The stated assumption allows ξ_t=16s/17, for which 2ξ_t+ξ_t² ≥ 32s/17 > s. So the displayed simplified rate does not follow from the hypothesis, whatever the value of s. The min{·} over an unspecified index is also ill-defined. The condition also forces ξ_t=0 when μ_tΔ_t=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant 16/17 by one that guarantees 2ξ_t+ξ_t² ≤ s (e.g. ξ_t ≤ s/3) and drop the meaningless min.
issues.overall_effect: The simplified contraction factor α_t and the quoted TIHT recovery condition δ<0.106 are not justified by the stated assumption. The general bound of Theorem thm:main_path is unaffected.
issues.title: Assumption on ξ_t does not imply the claimed simplification of the convergence factor
issues.why_classification: A short constant correction in the hypothesis restores the simplification, and nothing else in the paper depends on the exact constant.
